items.q: What is the primary anatomical site of origin for the vast majority of high-grade serous ovarian carcinomas (HGSOC)?
o: Fimbriated distal ends of the fallopian tubes (STIC lesions)
Mesonephric duct remnants in the broad ligament
items.exp: Overwhelming molecular and clinical evidence demonstrates that high-grade serous carcinoma originates predominantly from serous tubal intraepithelial carcinoma (STIC) precursor lesions within the mucosal lining of the fimbriated end of the fallopian tube, which exfoliate malignant cells that implant onto the ovary and peritoneum.
r: Correct. STIC lesions at the tubal fimbriae are the origin of high-grade serous ovarian carcinomas.
Incorrect. The ovarian surface epithelium was historically hypothesized, but disproven by modern genomic pathology.
Incorrect. Endometrial stroma gives rise to endometrial stromal sarcomas.
Incorrect. Mesonephric remnants give rise to rare Wolffian neoplasms.
items.kp: High-grade serous ovarian cancer originates from serous tubal intraepithelial carcinoma (STIC) lesions in the fallopian tube fimbriae.

items.q: A 55-year-old postmenopausal woman has an adnexal mass. Pelvic ultrasound reveals a 7 cm bilateral multiloculated cystic mass with solid papillary projections and moderate ascites (Ultrasound score = 3). Her serum CA-125 level is 120 U/mL. What is her Risk of Malignancy Index (RMI) score?
items.exp: The Risk of Malignancy Index is calculated as RMI = U x M x CA-125. The ultrasound score U = 3 (due to multiple malignant features). Menopausal status M = 3 (postmenopausal). Serum CA-125 = 120. Therefore, RMI = 3 x 3 x 120 = 1,080. A score > 200 mandates referral to a gynaecological oncology tertiary center.
r: Correct. RMI = 3 (ultrasound) x 3 (postmenopausal) x 120 (CA-125) = 1,080.
Incorrect. 360 incorrectly uses M = 1 for a postmenopausal patient.
Incorrect. 120 ignores the ultrasound and menopausal multipliers.
Incorrect. 2,400 miscalculates the product.
items.kp: Risk of Malignancy Index (RMI) = U x M x CA-125; a score > 200 warrants tertiary gynae-oncology referral.

items.q: Under the FIGO (2014) staging system for ovarian cancer, what stage corresponds to pleural effusion with cytologically confirmed malignant cells?
items.exp: FIGO Stage IV is divided into: Stage IVA, defined as pleural effusion with positive cytology for malignant cells; and Stage IVB, defined as parenchymal liver or splenic metastases, extra-abdominal organ metastases (e.g., lungs, bone, brain), and transmural intestinal involvement.
r: Correct. Malignant pleural effusion with positive cytology is classified as FIGO Stage IVA.
Incorrect. Stage IVB requires parenchymal organ metastases or extra-abdominal metastases.
Incorrect. Stage IIIC represents macroscopic peritoneal metastasis > 2 cm outside the pelvis or positive retroperitoneal nodes.
Incorrect. Stage IIB represents pelvic organ extension.
items.kp: Ovarian cancer with cytologically proven malignant pleural effusion is FIGO Stage IVA.

items.q: What is the single most important independent surgical prognostic factor for overall survival in patients with advanced epithelial ovarian cancer undergoing primary cytoreduction?
o: Complete cytoreduction with zero macroscopic residual disease (R0)
items.exp: Extensive meta-analyses and prospective clinical trials consistently confirm that the diameter of residual tumor following primary cytoreductive surgery is the most powerful modifiable prognostic variable. Patients with complete resection (R0, zero visible residual macroscopic disease) demonstrate the longest median overall survival (exceeding 60-70 months).
r: Correct. Complete cytoreduction (R0, no macroscopic residual tumor) is the strongest determinant of prolonged survival.
Incorrect. Operative duration does not independently predict survival.
Incorrect. Preserving the ovary in advanced cancer violates oncologic principles.
Incorrect. Appendectomy is only routine in mucinous histology and does not govern overall survival.
items.kp: Complete cytoreduction to zero macroscopic residual disease (R0) provides the highest survival in advanced ovarian cancer.

items.q: Which targeted pharmacological agent provides profound progression-free survival benefit as maintenance therapy in women with advanced high-grade serous ovarian cancer harboring a BRCA1 or BRCA2 mutation?
items.exp: PARP inhibitors (e.g., olaparib, niraparib, rucaparib) exploit synthetic lethality in tumors with homologous recombination deficiency (such as BRCA1/2 mutations). Inhibiting PARP prevents single-strand base excision repair; in BRCA-deficient cells lacking double-strand break repair, lethal DNA damage accumulates, inducing selective tumor apoptosis.
r: Correct. Olaparib is a PARP inhibitor approved for maintenance in BRCA-mutated ovarian cancer via synthetic lethality.
Incorrect. Trastuzumab targets HER2, which is rarely amplified in epithelial ovarian cancer.
Incorrect. Tamoxifen has modest activity in recurrent low-grade disease, not first-line maintenance.
Incorrect. Pembrolizumab has limited monotherapy activity in HGSOC without high microsatellite instability.
items.kp: PARP inhibitors like olaparib exploit synthetic lethality in BRCA-mutated ovarian cancers to dramatically prolong progression-free survival.

items.q: A 19-year-old nulliparous woman is found to have an intact, unruptured 9 cm right ovarian mass confined to the right ovary. Peritoneal washings are negative, and staging biopsies show no extra-ovarian spread. Histology reveals Stage IA dysgerminoma. What is the standard fertility-sparing surgical management?
o: Right salpingo-oophorectomy with preservation of the uterus and left ovary, plus surgical staging
Total abdominal hysterectomy and bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy
Right ovarian cystectomy with enucleation only
Radiation therapy to the whole pelvis
items.exp: Malignant germ cell tumors (such as dysgerminoma) occur predominantly in young adolescents and women. In Stage IA disease, fertility-sparing surgery consisting of unilateral salpingo-oophorectomy, peritoneal washings, omentectomy, and retroperitoneal lymph node assessment, while preserving the uterus and contralateral normal ovary, is the standard of care with > 95% cure rates.
r: Correct. Unilateral salpingo-oophorectomy preserving the uterus and contralateral adnexa is standard for Stage IA germ cell tumors.
Incorrect. Hysterectomy and bilateral oophorectomy causes permanent sterility and is unnecessary in Stage IA germ cell tumors.
Incorrect. Simple cystectomy carries high recurrence and rupture risk for malignant neoplasms.
Incorrect. Radiation causes permanent ovarian failure and uterine fibrosis.
items.kp: Stage IA malignant ovarian germ cell tumors are managed with fertility-sparing unilateral salpingo-oophorectomy and surgical staging.

items.q: Which tumor marker is characteristically elevated in malignant ovarian endodermal sinus (yolk sac) tumors?
items.exp: Yolk sac tumors (endodermal sinus tumors) synthesize alpha-fetoprotein (AFP), which serves as a highly sensitive and specific diagnostic and surveillance serum biomarker. Histology characteristically reveals Schiller-Duval bodies.
r: Correct. Alpha-fetoprotein (AFP) is the definitive tumor marker for ovarian yolk sac tumors.
Incorrect. CA-125 is a marker for epithelial serous ovarian carcinoma.
Incorrect. Beta-hCG is secreted by choriocarcinoma and embryonal carcinoma.
Incorrect. Inhibin B is secreted by granulosa cell tumors.
items.kp: Ovarian yolk sac (endodermal sinus) tumors secrete alpha-fetoprotein (AFP) and display Schiller-Duval bodies on histology.

items.q: What is the recommended risk-reducing surgical procedure for women with confirmed BRCA1 germline mutations after completion of childbearing (typically around age 35 to 40)?
o: Routine transvaginal ultrasound screening every 3 months
items.exp: In BRCA1 mutation carriers (lifetime ovarian cancer risk 39-44%), risk-reducing bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy (RRSO) between age 35 and 40 reduces ovarian/fallopian cancer risk by 80-90% and reduces all-cause mortality. Because precursor lesions arise in the fimbria, complete salpingo-oophorectomy (with serial sectioning of tubes) is mandatory.
r: Correct. Bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy is the standard risk-reducing intervention for BRCA1 carriers.
Incorrect. Tubal ligation provides modest protection but leaves the vulnerable fimbriae in situ.
Incorrect. Hysterectomy alone leaves the ovaries and fallopian tubes, failing to prevent cancer.
Incorrect. Screening with ultrasound and CA-125 has failed to reduce mortality in randomized screening trials.
items.kp: Risk-reducing bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy (RRSO) is the gold standard for reducing ovarian cancer mortality in BRCA1 carriers.

items.q: Which histological subtype of ovarian carcinoma is most strongly associated with pelvic endometriosis and harbors frequent mutations in the ARID1A tumor suppressor gene?
items.exp: Clear cell carcinoma and endometrioid carcinoma of the ovary are strongly associated with pre-existing ovarian endometriosis (endometrioma). Loss-of-function somatic mutations in ARID1A and activating mutations in PIK3CA are found in over 50% of clear cell carcinomas and in adjacent endometriotic precursor implants.
r: Correct. Clear cell carcinoma arises in endometriosis and characteristically exhibits ARID1A mutations.
Incorrect. High-grade serous arises from tubal STIC and harbors TP53 mutations.
Incorrect. Mucinous carcinoma harbors KRAS mutations and is unrelated to endometriosis.
Incorrect. Brenner tumors are rare urothelial-like epithelial neoplasms.
items.kp: Ovarian clear cell carcinoma is strongly associated with endometriosis and frequently harbors ARID1A mutations.

items.q: A 60-year-old woman with advanced ovarian cancer has biopsy-proven tumor deposits measuring 3 cm across the surface of the transverse colon and retroperitoneal para-aortic lymph node metastases. What FIGO stage is this?
items.exp: Under FIGO (2014) criteria, Stage III involves peritoneal metastasis beyond the pelvis and/or retroperitoneal lymph node metastases: Stage IIIA is microscopic peritoneal spread; Stage IIIB is macroscopic peritoneal metastasis <= 2 cm; and Stage IIIC is macroscopic peritoneal metastasis > 2 cm outside the pelvis, or retroperitoneal lymph node metastasis.
r: Correct. Peritoneal metastases > 2 cm outside the pelvis or positive retroperitoneal nodes define FIGO Stage IIIC.
Incorrect. Stage IIIB is restricted to macroscopic deposits <= 2 cm.
Incorrect. Stage IIB is confined within the true pelvis.
Incorrect. Stage IVB requires parenchymal organ or extra-abdominal metastases.
items.kp: Peritoneal metastases greater than 2 cm outside the pelvis or retroperitoneal lymph node metastases define FIGO Stage IIIC.
